title: Hán
capsule: The Kingdom of Hán (written with an extra letter to distinguish it from the Han dynasty) was the fief Xiang Yu allowed King Cheng to retain in 206 BC over part of the former Warring States territory of Han, with its capital at Yangzhai. Unlike most of the Eighteen Kingdoms' rulers, Han Cheng was a scion of the old Warring States Han royal house rather than a rebel general. Xiang Yu grew distrustful of him, never let him take up his fief, and had him executed later that year, installing his own follower Zheng Chang as king — who was soon defeated by Liu Bang's forces and surrendered, helping trigger the wider collapse of the Eighteen Kingdoms settlement.
